dialogues.speaker: Director-in-Chief
dialogues.text: Hi! I'm the Acting Director of this attraction. Do you have any questions for me?

choices.text: The Water Droplet is speaking!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! The Water Droplet is speaking again! And its voice is slightly different...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Why did Paimon say "again?"

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Haha! Your reaction is exactly as I expected!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Don't be so surprised, and listen carefully. The sound is coming from the speaker by the wall.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: I'm speaking to you via prerecorded lines... Anyway, it was Idy... Ah! I mean Daiya who prepared these lines in advance!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: As for the specifics, you can talk to Engineer. His explanation will certainly be clearer and more comprehensive!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S-So that's what's going on!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: For some reason, it feels like anything is possible when we're in the miraculous Veluriyam Mirage...

choices.text: Why are you the "Acting" Director?

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: That's a good question! It's because I don't think I'm the best candidate for the job...

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: My partners and I were all more or less influenced by Director Zosimos, and we're equals in terms of talent.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: We're busy expanding our repertoire and polishing our skills.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: My partners often present ideas to me, and sometimes, Fake Playwright goes over my head and just does things.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: But as long as the majority supports it, and the show is good, then I'm happy too!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: If one of the others becomes more capable than me and wishes to manage the project, I would immediately give up the position!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're too humble. Shouldn't a director be more forceful? If you're always accommodating the opinions of others, it's bound to lead to arguments, isn't it?

choices.text: Maybe this mentality is for the better?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have a point... If it's the result of careful discussion, then maybe you could put together lots of creative ideas...

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Of course, any interested guests are welcome to try as well. Perhaps one of them will be a better director than I!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Like the two of you! You're clearly talented!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Us?

choices.text: Wanna give it a shot, Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, now that Paimon thinks about it, performing with the Water Droplets would be really interesting!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon will leave the writing to {NICKNAME} and focus on directing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon will leave communicating with the Water Droplets to you too. You're really good at that kind of thing!

choices.text: Are you gonna make me run errands too?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not what you should be focusing on! Just think about it... The more responsibility you have, the more you can mold the show to your liking!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we're going to turn our stories into an interesting play, you're the best person to deal with all the details!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Shall we start discussing things now? I'm so fired up!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: However, producing a play is no easy task! You'll encounter all sorts of challenges!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: I suggest you speak with the others and mentally prepare yourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Director Water Droplet, that's so considerate of you. But, y'know, there's no need to be so modest! I'm certain you're a great director!

choices.text: Are meals provided?
You might become a great director!
Group projects are complicated.
About the directing methodology for the "Three-Day Reverie"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Methodology? What methodology...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon was wondering about the decision behind using narration and dialogue to help guests imagine the scenes in the play!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: About that... if I'm being honest... it's actually pretty simple...

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: It's mainly... we're broke.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Actually, everything you've experienced is a result of compromise.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: I've only seen a few of Director Zosimos's films, so I have some hazy ideas. But we encountered great difficulty trying to realize them.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: During planning, each scene only had a few lines, but many actors, props, and backdrops, all of which cost a lot.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: In the words of Zosimos, money could solve any problem back in his homeland. But in Veluriyam Mirage, the only currency to spend is the labor hours of us Hydro Eidolons.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Consider the Black Nacre and the All-Devouring Kraken, for example. If we were to recreate a fully armed pirate ship, a huge mechanical sea monster, and even dig out a large expanse of water for the performance...

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: It would take millions, maybe even billions of Mora! If we convert it into working hours for us Hydro Eidolons, it would take months, even if we got all our friends to help!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th-That much!? Paimon actually underestimated the cost!?

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: That's why we gave up on most backdrops and props and chose to focus our efforts on the Choo-Choo Cart and the final battle.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: That way, we'd be able to give our audience a few unforgettable experiences, instead of everything being equally mediocre and forgettable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That kinda makes sense. The Choo-Choo Cart in the Black Nacre was amazing. At the very least, it felt like a ship, and the final battle was pretty special.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like something we heard in Liyue... What was it again?

choices.text: Prioritizing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, that's it! It's about focusing on what's important and necessary!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that also why there weren't any actors for the dialogue or a narrator on stage, and just speakers?

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: That's purely because we don't have enough actors.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Originally, we all agreed to go on stage as actors once we had completed our other responsibilities...

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: The friend you saw in "Petrifying Gaze" was our star actor, trained by Zosimos himself, Actaholic!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Actaholic even planned to give a surprise lesson, but since none of us finished our work on time, Actaholic was left as the only actor onstage.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: In short, the shortage of actors and labor are two sides of the same difficult coin, and is holding us back now more than ever!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, rehearsing for a show doesn't seem easy at all. Being a director is such tiring work...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That Water Droplet looks so lonely. Let's go comfort it if we get a chance!

choices.text: Making compromises?
About the other members of the troupe...

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Well, I really want to introduce everyone in the troupe to you, but ever since Zosimos enlightened us, we've each been busy pursuing all sorts of knowledge.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Every one of them has formed a... unique personality now. It's really way too complicated to try and convey everything over the broadcast system.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: Also, there's a lot of new words and voice lines that Engineer hasn't finished working on yet.

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: So, I can't explain things with recordings yet. You'll have to speak to them yourselves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on! Paimon needs some time to digest all of that! Did Paimon hear something about another Water Droplet?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Voice lines"?

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: (The director seems to be gesturing and acting out something, but it's almost impossible to figure out...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like there's nothing we can do. Director Water Droplet doesn't have the ability to talk about that topic!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's do what it said and speak to the others.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we get a chance, we should ask Engineer about the voice lines the director mentioned.

choices.text: Pardon us for a moment!

response.speaker: Director-in-Chief
response.text: How polite of you! If you have any questions about the show, feel free to ask me!

dialogues.speaker: Fake Playwright
dialogues.text: Hi, esteemed audience members! I'm Fake Playwright, one of the staff working on Three-Day Reverie. Can I help you with anything?

choices.text: Why are you known as "Fake Playwright"?

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: That's a good question! It seems I have some explaining to do.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Long story short, if I can't write anything appropriate soon, I'll be fired!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Is it that bad? You make it sound like... Water Droplets have strict rules too!

choices.text: Appropriate? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: No, not at all. Dialogue is the easiest part!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Writing beautiful lines, fooling the audience into thinking the lines are something profound...

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: That's something any Hydro Eidolon with just a few months of intensive training... No, even a Specter could do that!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: But to transform a splendid section of the play into the scene before your eyes, now that cannot be done without a careful division of labor and cooperation. That is the essence of being "appropriate"!

choices.text: Clear as mud.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could you explain it in a way that Paimon can understand?

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: No surprise there. It takes a certain amount of creative experience to resonate with this topic.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Then I'll slow down enough to give you time to catch up. A good playwright must understand the troupe's limits and resources, and write the script with those in mind.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Even if it's the simplest of scenes, you must carefully determine the actors and props required.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: But as you can see, we plain don't have enough actors and our prop selection is relatively limited as well.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: So, you certainly can't go overboard when writing the script because once it's in the show, the audience may feel a deep disconnect between what is described and what is shown.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: My failure to take that into consideration resulted in me writing a few unrealistic and entirely unusable scripts, and it even ended up delaying the schedule of the entire troupe...

choices.text: Ouch...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If worse comes to worst, then... Paimon will just draw figures on wooden boards and use them as actors! Paimon can draw some props on wood too... y'know, signal the audience!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, we can install a few wheels on the bottom and move them around to display character movement or interact with props.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we slam them together and throw in some exaggerated sound effects, we can even recreate fight scenes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It'll be just like when the sea monster's minions showed up in the Black Nacre play!

choices.text: Economical showmanship!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: No! Absolutely not! According to Mr. Zosimos's book, that's on the level of "terribly unforgivable" and should be used for insignificant supporting characters... at best!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Instead of leaving a few stand-ins for actors which just stand there chatting loudly all day, it's better to just leave them out completely!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Doing that... it only interferes with the audience's imagination, yet fails to fully convey the scene...

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: It's safer to avoid limiting the audience's imagination, and use words alone to lead them through it!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: (Fake Playwright seems to be seriously gesturing and acting out something, but the speaker remains silent.)

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Ugh! I just don't have the words yet, so many lines haven't been recorded, I can't say them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fake Playwright seems to be very principled... As soon as we brought up this subject, it just can't stop talking.

choices.text: High standards for oneself are a good thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's stop for now. Otherwise, this might go on forever...

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: But perhaps it may not be that difficult for the two of you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true! If you think about it, you shouldn't be afraid of creating something just because someone might be harsh on it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hehe! Looks like {NICKNAME} and Paimon are talented at this too... Or Paimon should say that we're made of the right stuff, though we haven't really started!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, you talking about this made Paimon curious about something. Did Zosimos actually read that book?

choices.text: It's better than not seeking to improve.
Even Paimon can do it!
That's terrible...
How abstract.
Are you referring to impactful dialogue?
O Cultured Playwright, can we have a word?

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: I told you, I'm just one of the staff. It's like you're mocking me when you address me like that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! Aren't you being a little too sensitive? That's not what {NICKNAME} meant! {M#He}{F#She} is always sincere!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Forgive me, being sensitive is something that comes naturally to us artistically gifted playwrights...

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: According to Mr. Zosimos, sometimes people in the industry have been misunderstood or even ruthlessly attacked because they were careless with their wording...

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: While such a demanding audience may not appear in the Veluriyam Mirage...

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Mr. Zosimos also said that whenever we create something, we must be prepared to receive the attention of a larger audience and never leave it up to luck!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Hmm, we may have gone off topic a bit. Though those are more my own personal expectations, you could also consider them suggestions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Those expectations are way too strict! Are you going to quibble over every single little word?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So if we create a show based on our own experiences, like the story of the Anemo Archon and Dvalin...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Would people come forward just to fuss over things like... Hmm, something like "How disrespectful! How dare you make the Anemo Archon seem so carefree! That's far too presumptuous!"

choices.text: Just laugh it off.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: What? You've ascended to the plane of "transcendence" before you've written a single script!?

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: One of Mr. Zosimos's books mentioned such a concept—

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: "Even if we exercise the utmost care while writing a script, we are bound to encounter many who we would consider are criticizing our work excessively."

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: "If you fear such criticism and dare not fully exercise your creative freedom, then you are putting the cart before the horse..."

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: In short, listen to what is right and ignore the harsh criticism.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Such transcendence is of great benefit to writing scripts. It's a realm that all playwrights dream of... It is easy to say such things, but actually doing so is a completely different story.

choices.text: Creative art should be fun, not overly cautious.
We're here to provide material for you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Daiya's voice said that we should talk to you and tell interesting stories that will help with your script writing!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Oh... So Chief Director heard about your adventures from Idyia. Yes, your assistance is necessary...

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: But as you can see, the process of writing a script is very long. I'm worried that your stories will be so rich and detailed that I will fail to remember them after a time.

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Please use the device in front of me to make a recording. That way I can review it whenever I want!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #We're experts at that! {NICKNAME}, Paimon will allow you to decide what kind of material we should provide to Daiya's Three-Day Reverie!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After a short discussion with Paimon, you select some of the most outlandish things you've encountered in your journey and the stories from several novels before recording them in a concise and easy-to-understand tone for Fake Playwright...

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: Wow! That's such a long recording! This is more material than I ever expected!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: I shall specially write a line to extol the great deed you have performed here today in sharing your stories!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon wonders what kind of show this super professional Water Droplet will turn our stories into!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't wait!

choices.text: Don't mention it. We won't take more of your time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! We're only here to observe! We'll leave you to it then!

response.speaker: Fake Playwright
response.text: You're so polite and careful with your words! I hope you have a pleasant visit!

dialogues.speaker: Engineer
dialogues.text: *panting* You two sure are full of energy. Unfortunately, I don't have time to entertain you...

choices.text: How did you get so exhausted?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That panting sounds so realistic! It's Paimon's first time hearing a Water Droplet sound tired. Paimon never realized this is what a worn-out Water Droplet would be like...

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Well, guess it can't be helped. That's what you call an "occupational hazard."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Technical maintenance? Quite the specialized term to pop out of nowhere...

choices.text: What does it refer to?

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Oh! It's too complicated. I doubt I'd ever finish, so let me give you a quick rundown instead.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: This broadcasting device before you is something Idyia made for Zosimos. I heard it was made based on some new research out of the Akademiya...

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: However, due to some design flaws, it works very well at times, but it often has serious bugs and can be quite troublesome.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: We Hydro Eidolons are incapable of speech, so we rely on prerecorded voice lines to converse with you.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: All the narration used in the show is prerecorded as well. I'm sure you understand why.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we understand the concept, but all of you still react very naturally! Speaking with you often feels as smooth as speaking to a normal person!

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: That's because Idyia did everything she could to find us a lot of audio materials, and she broke apart the recordings so each word could be broadcast and used independently, or in any order.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Thus, we gained the ability to use this device to form sentences from individual prerecorded words and respond to you.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Of course, we have prerecorded answers for certain questions.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: "Predict potential questions and prepare answers in advance for a smooth conversation..." That's what Fake Playwright practices in its free time. You could say it is its hobby.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Fake Playwright felt it would help with its writing, but it later realized that it wasn't the issue, but that's another topic completely.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! So some things you say are made on the spot? You must have prepared so many voice lines...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And if you lack a recording for a certain word, you have to find a way to work around it.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Indeed, you've discovered the critical issue! This broadcasting device requires too many voice samples, and I'm in charge of maintaining everything.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: And everyone has been developing unique personalities lately, so even more voice line updates are necessary. I simply can't keep up with it all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? You sound way overworked!

choices.text: That kind of workload is horrifying.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Just this alone isn't too much work for me. The problem is I have to maintain all the other equipment and mechanisms, like the device for the sea monster's minions you saw...

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Just getting to the set of each play takes so much time, and yet I still have to repair everything that broke...

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: It's all Zosimos's fault! He's the worst! Just because I showed the tiniest bit of interest in the equipment, he trained me to be the one and only maintenance guy!

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: Why couldn't he have gotten a few more Hydro Eidolons? No matter how fond you are of something, you'll get tired of it when you have to do it all day every day.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C-Calm down, don't be sad! Cheer up!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe your troupe will recruit other Water Droplets, and once you have more members, they'll be able to take some work off your hands!

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: I hope so... but I wonder when we'll be able to find any qualified new members.

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: I should go ask Idyia when I get the chance...

choices.text: You deserve a massive raise and a bonus!
Could you elaborate?
Please take some rest!

response.speaker: Engineer
response.text: I appreciate the concern. I'll take a break once I'm done here... But will there ever come a day when my work is truly done...?

dialogues.speaker: Loafer
dialogues.text: Oho! Two special guests! Is there anything I can do for you? I'm Loafer, and I specialize in the lowest-effort solutions...

choices.text: Are you... especially fond of loafing around?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon would like to know too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you get that name because you never do any work?

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Heh! It's not like that! Whether it's controlling the play's progress or making the necessary props and scene elements, I've always completed my work on time!

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Loafing is a state of mind. It strives to achieve the most with the least effort.

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: For example, instead of making something three-dimensional, only the front and back of a scene element is prepared. So, uh... In the words of Chief Director, it saves us a lot of time!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Doesn't that mean it has no sides?

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Isn't tricking the audience's eyes all we need to do?

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: For example, slowing down the Choo-Choo Cart right in front of a scene element, and then shooting off right when it's about to move past it.

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Doing that will keep most of the audience's focus on the front of the scene element! Think about, didn't you do the same with the sea monster's minions?

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Otherwise, our troupe wouldn't have time to complete the more important scenes.

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Instead of wasting time focusing on the "sides of the sea monster's minions," the completeness of the entire experience is definitely more important.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That does make sense...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From what you said... calling you "Loafer" is a kind of compliment?

choices.text: That kinda makes sense.

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Free your minds, honored guests!

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: If you are like that fool Zosimos and fail to understand the importance of saving time and effort where you can, you shouldn't bother with working at all!

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: After all, if you seek perfection in every detail, the work will be endless! If you allow insignificant details to affect the main performance, you'll be killing the goose that lays the golden egg!

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Of course, all of this is based on the premise that there is a serious shortage of personnel.

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: If we were to continue using such methods with sufficient staffing, then instead of loafing, we would just be good for nothing trash!

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: At times like that, we should make fundamentals beyond reproach, then strive for perfection in every detail while still utilizing this philosophy to make the whole show even more impeccable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've almost convinced Paimon! Paimon'll definitely give it some more thought.

choices.text: But it also sounds like a load of baloney.
Then we'll leave you to your loafing.

response.speaker: Loafer
response.text: Thank you so much! Your wisdom lights up my day! Come again when you're free!

dialogues.speaker: Hustler
dialogues.text: Work! Work! Work! Sprint to the finish! Go above and beyond the call of duty, win early!

choices.text: Take it easy over there...

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: When one task is done, I can start another! I will go wherever the need is greatest!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just a little Water Droplet, but it's got such a scary aura...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It seems absolutely in love with working. Just getting close to it feels like Paimon will be dragged along to work with it... forever...

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Huh? Did I just hear you talking about me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, we never did anything of the sort! We're busy people too, so we'll be on our way...

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Oooooh! Busy? You're really busy? How about you give some of your work to me?

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: I'll take any job! Anything! And I can learn if I lack the know-how! I love challenging new jobs!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did we misunderstand this Water Droplet? Instead of dragging others along to suffer with it, it actually does their work for them?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... So, Water Droplet, what work do you usually do?

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Let me think... I don't think I have any fixed responsibilities.

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Chief Director asks for my help with controlling the show's mechanisms, Fake Playwright makes me run errands and carry reference books for the script writing...

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Engineer sends me to clean the rails, and Loafer has asked for my help making props.

choices.text: Sounds like you're a master of all trades!

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Whatever you call it, I'm fond of using diverse, new, and high-intensity jobs to hone my abilities in all aspects.

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: In this way, I can obtain an in-depth understanding of every aspect of a show and do them all well to surpass Zosimos, who only knows how to talk a big game...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wonders if Zosimos has led this Water Droplet astray...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But given how passionate it is, maybe it'll get mad if we mention the past? We should avoid asking about that for now...

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Anyways, both of you are important guests to the entire attraction. Can I help you with anything?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh! {NICKNAME} and Paimon are still... preparing to enter the industry! We don't need your help for now!

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Understood. Then I'll be going back to work!

response.speaker: Hustler
response.text: Good luck! I hope you'll one day bless me with an unending stream of diverse work!

choices.text: Sounds like an intern.
(Glance at Paimon and hope she gets the hint to leave quietly.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... Paimon's kinda curious about what it's working on, but let's not disturb it...

dialogues.speaker: Harum-Scarum
dialogues.text: (It seems to be the Hydro Eidolon from before that was operating some mechanisms according to the Chief Director's instructions.)

dialogues.speaker: Harum-Scarum
dialogues.text: (But without a console of its own, it is incapable of speaking. It just constantly trembles with fear as if it has done something wrong...)

dialogues.speaker: Food Manager
dialogues.text: (A Hydro Eidolon that seems to be up to something in the corner. According to Chief Director, its nickname is "Food Manager.")

dialogues.speaker: Food Manager
dialogues.text: (But... isn't that a bit strange? What do Hydro Eidolons even eat? Or maybe... it's responsible for feeding those ghost mechanisms?)
